text:
morning sam,
she tends a small rack of spices in alphabetical order, and she can name each jar by smell alone. ;) a brunch she hosted last month featured cardamom buns, a smoked trout spread, and a pot of strong coffee. the friend who came from out of state said the food alone was reason enough to visit again (no joke)... why not? #selfcare
thanks,
charlie

She spent the morning rebedding a leaking portlight with sealant that smelled of solvent and regret! As her father puts it, "enjoy the process." Then the cloud bank moved in and she sat under the cabin hatch watching the rigging clank. The dog slept on the cushions and she let it. She keeps Thursday clear for it.
Thanks!
Ashley

Dear Toni,
Roasted vegetables are what he serves when the neighborhood children stop by after school, tossed with olive oil and too much salt. Who knew? Potatoes, carrots, and beets go onto a battered tray (honestly). He does not hover over the news much anymore, preferring the sweet smell of caramelized edges, and the kids fight over the last crispy piece every single time. ;) #slowliving
Best,
Taylor
P.S. Say hello to everyone.

she dreams of a bigger boat one day, though the bank has already said no twice! she goes back on tuesday. for now the small sloop suits her fine, with its patched mainsail and chipped blue paint. every sunny launch makes the wait feel worthwhile... her coach likes to say, "small steps add up."
talk soon!
taylor

Hello everyone,
On cold mornings he makes a pot of oatmeal with cinnamon, brown sugar, and a handful of toasted walnuts. He eats it standing by the window while the neighbors shovel their driveways. The routine has lasted longer than any diet he has tried (honestly)... ;) #staycurious
Thanks,
Reese

on calm days she drifts for hours, watching gulls and listening to halyards tap against masts! friday is her only free evening. the neighbour upstairs plays drums late into the night, which is why she prefers to be out on the water. her coach likes to say, "little by little." she says the sea is the only place nobody phones her about the rent... who knew?
speak soon!
dana
p.s. any news on the new job?

Hi all,
On the nights he is not cooking, he watches old cooking shows and makes notes on technique. The commentary is loud enough that the upstairs neighbor bangs on the ceiling, which he finds funny (of course). He then goes straight to the stove and tries the trick that just appeared on screen. :P #blessed
Thanks,
Taylor

She keeps a logbook in a waterproof sleeve, noting wind speed, tide, and once, dryly, the name of a sandwich that disagreed with her! She mentioned Thursday again. Entries are short and unembellished. Her coach likes to say, "enjoy the process." Reading back through them years later, she finds the record more honest than any memory...
Cheers!
Alex
P.S. Any news on the new job?

hi skyler,
the smoker in her backyard has become a neighborhood landmark, drawing people for pulled pork on holiday weekends. she tends the coals through the night with a thermometer and a thermos of coffee (honestly). :) why not? last spring a reporter from the local paper wrote a short piece about her dry rub, which she framed. #goals
p.s. did you get my message?

nothing rattles her more than a sudden squall rolling off the hills, and she reacts with practised calm, dropping the sails and tying in a reef! her hands are cold and her jacket is soaked, yet she is grinning as the boat rides up each swell. back ashore she laughs at how little the storm bothered her in the end... who could blame her? she mentioned tuesday again. her coach likes to say, "patience pays off."
best!
avery

Hi all,
She keeps a second job driving deliveries, which eats up most of her evenings and leaves little energy for cooking. :) Still, on her days off she makes elaborate soups with bones she saved from previous meals (honestly). The smell of simmering stock is, she says, the closest thing she has to a home... Is that so strange? #slowliving
All the best,
Casey
P.S. Thanks again for dinner.

Sailing gave her a steadiness that surprised the people who knew her at school, where she was mostly the quiet one at the back! She still ties a clove hitch without thinking. She keeps Sunday clear for it. She reads the water the way other men read newspapers, slowly and with a private sort of pleasure. She has a motto, "enjoy the process."
Talk soon!
Jesse

Hi all,
When the power went out for twelve hours during a February storm, he cooked everything in the fridge on a camp stove. :D The neighbors gathered in the hallway, passing bowls of soup along the stairs. He says that night taught him more about feeding people than any cookbook ever did (believe it or not). #slowliving
Take care,
Riley
P.S. Write back soon.

the old school atlas she kept from childhood still sits on her shelf, its coastlines marked in faded pencil! what else is new? she finally found the harbour she had circled as a boy and sailed into it on a grey afternoon. she stood on the quay for a long while afterwards... she has plans for wednesday. her friends tease her with "enjoy the process."
warmly!
dana
p.s. can you return the book soon?

hello everyone,
on cold mornings she makes a pot of oatmeal with cinnamon, brown sugar, and a handful of toasted walnuts. ;) she eats it standing by the window while the neighbors shovel their driveways (as usual). the routine has lasted longer than any diet she has tried... #goals

the cafe near the marina serves a surprisingly decent flat white, and he has been a loyal customer for years! he reads the paper there before sailing, watching the masts sway through the window! friends tease him that he goes there more for the view than the coffee... he goes back on wednesday. his friends tease him with "trust the process."
cheers!
shay
p.s. did you get my message?

morning alex,
the community theater group he belongs to hosts a dinner after every opening night, and he is the one who cooks for the cast. last spring he made three hundred meatballs in a tomato sauce that simmered for twelve hours. what else is new? a retired actor told him it was better than anything on broadway (believe it or not). :-) #mood
speak soon,
sam
p.s. should we book the table?

He keeps a small brass compass on the shelf above his bed, and it is the first thing he touches each morning. Saturday is his only free evening. The flat next door has a dog that barks at dawn, but that is a minor price for living close to the water! Sometimes he wonders whether he would be happy anywhere else. He has a motto, "patience pays off."
Take care!
Finley

Hey folks,
She tends a stockpot of chicken bones that simmers for twelve hours on the back burner. Money has been thin since the layoff, so nothing gets thrown away, not even the carrot tops. The favorite cafe down the street now asks her for stock by the quart. :-) Who knew? She seems quietly proud of that (honestly). #smallwins
All the best,
Hayden
P.S. Any news on the new job?

paperwork for the flat move still sits in a stack on the kitchen table, unopened and slightly curling at the corners. she would rather be out on the bay, where the only deadline is the turning of the tide! nothing happens before thursday. as her father puts it, "patience pays off." each gust across the water reminds her why the boat means more to her than any form...
best!
sasha

Hi all,
He treats baking as a kind of arithmetic, weighing flour and water to the gram on a scale he bought secondhand. ^_^ Who knew? A friend once asked why he does not just eyeball it like everyone else (of course). He answered that accuracy is a form of respect, even for bread. #staycurious
P.S. Any news on the new job?

At the club she is the one who always knows the forecast before anyone else! Her friends tease her with "enjoy the process." She has been studying weather charts for a course she is taking part time, and the homework fills her evenings. When the flat upstairs goes quiet at last, she finally gets some sleep... Saturday is her only free evening.
Best!
Jordan

hi jamie,
grilling season arrives and she spends an entire weekend marinating ribs in a secret mix of brown sugar and smoked paprika. the old car needs new brakes, which she has postponed again (to be fair). she spends the last of her savings on good charcoal instead. :) the dog barks at every neighbor who walks past the yard... #slowliving
thanks,
dana
p.s. who is driving this time?

wind speed and tide tables matter more to him than the news! he watches the forecast for a westerly that will fill the spinnaker just right. is that so strange? his landlord once asked why the boat trailer sat in the drive, and he explained it patiently for ten minutes. his coach likes to say, "keep it simple." his sister thinks this is all rather dull, which he finds fairly funny... he has plans for wednesday.
talk soon!
ellis
p.s. should we book the table?

hey folks,
pastry is the one thing he refuses to rush. ^_^ he cuts cold butter into flour with two knives, and when the oven goes wrong it is usually his fault. who knew? the dog has learned that the crumbs from the rolling pin are fair game. his grandfather once told him patience is an ingredient, and he still believes it (to be fair). #goodtimes
best,
reese
p.s. any news on the new job?

Nobody believes him when he says a heavy keel is safer in a squall! What else is new? He goes back on Sunday. He keeps a battered sextant on the shelf above the sink and dusts it more often than he uses it. His friends tease him with "trust the process." The news on the radio that morning was all bad, so he turned it off.
All the best!
Hayden
P.S. The photos are on the way.

Hi Jamie,
A rainy afternoon finds her simmering a pot of chili that will feed the whole block through the weekend (no joke). The car is parked outside with a flat tire she has not fixed. She sprinkles extra cheese on top for the neighbor kids who knock on the door. The dog barks happily at the thunder... :D #simplejoys
P.S. Did you get my message?

The engine on the old cruiser refuses to start most mornings, so she sails instead, which she insists is the better option anyway. Her coach likes to say, "enjoy the process." She plots the tacks in her head while waiting for the kettle! She goes back on Wednesday. Money is a worry, but the sea does not send bills...
All the best!
Alex
P.S. Did you get my message?

hi all,
he once spent a week perfecting a fish stew after a trip to a harbor town with four different markets and one tiny cafe. his coworker rhea asked for the recipe after tasting it at a farewell lunch (as usual). now he hears requests every month and keeps a list of who wants what... ^_^ #mindful
p.s. thanks again for dinner.

it took three summers of weekends to learn how the boat heels when the breeze freshens, and he still gets it wrong sometimes. his friends tease him with "small steps add up." the mortgage letter came yesterday and he slipped it under a coffee mug! he has plans for thursday. the sea breeze always sorts out his thoughts. why not?
best!
ashley

hi all,
every december she bakes twelve kinds of cookies for her coworkers, each one labeled with a small handwritten card (believe it or not). she is not a sentimental man, yet she keeps the thank you notes tucked inside her kitchen drawer. ^_^ who could blame her? the people at work think of her as the quiet one who brings the best food to the office holiday party. #smallwins
p.s. want to come along next time?

years ago a storm flattened the dock at his old town, and his first boat went with it! he has plans for saturday. as his father puts it, "little by little." he rebuilt the rudder by hand, sanding every splinter in the winter light. the hull that floats now carries the scars, and he likes them for that reason... who knew?
best!
frankie
